plan.name: Return sharded sandbox checks within the tool limit
plan.summary: Keep the agent's test tool and the factory's checks on the same Sandbox.Run path, with an embedded Python standard-library runner that first builds each touched package's test binary once, serially, then reuses those binaries for discovery, shards and acceptance checks from each package's directory; discover Test, Fuzz and Example entries, sort them by package and name and distribute them round-robin among eight concurrent workers, each running its package groups in order, so every discovered top-level test runs in exactly one touched-package shard and new tests join automatically. Keep the offline pinned container, localhost hostname and isolated shared build cache, retain 4 GiB and 1024 process limits per container (12 GiB and 3072 processes for three watcher steps), and limit Go compilation to one package at a time per command with GOMAXPROCS=2. Give the entire Sandbox.Run a ten-minute deadline from entry and each shard an eight-minute timeout, reserve another minute for startup and fifteen seconds for cleanup below both unchanged 900-second backend tool limits, stop the container on deadline, and return package-qualified partial test results and a summary naming passed, failed, still-running and unstarted tests; a failed build, shard, timeout or interrupted run fails the check while independent shards continue, and acceptance tests run afterward with their own package-qualified results under the same deadline. Update SPEC.md and README.md to describe these checks, limits and deadline reports, with changed SPEC bullets citing D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0113, D-0117, D-0122, D-0173, D-0189, D-0197 and D-0233 as applicable, and adapt the existing marker-ordering test's fixtures for compiled binaries while preserving its ordering assertions. This sharding and deadline policy needs a new decision that the merger records, and merger work also includes reloading the watchers and running INVARIANT_PLUMBING_REAL=1 go test ./internal/plumbing -run '^TestSandboxBudgetAndRealCheckout$' -count=1 -timeout 20m to confirm that three concurrent cold-cache real-image runs of the checkout pass within the chosen deadline and measured memory and process peaks stay within the limits, with internal/verify/verify.go named only in the real-image subtest's plan to exercise internal/verify while this change's external plumbing_test acceptance test stays in internal/plumbing.

tests.name: TestSandboxShardsEveryTopLevelTestExactlyOnce
tests.says: Each touched package is compiled once before shards start, and its binary is reused from its package directory for discovery, shards and acceptance checks; real fixture tests, examples and fuzz seeds run exactly once in eight simultaneous shards assigned by sorted round-robin discovery, with subtests intact, a newly added test included, empty packages allowed and the chosen container limits enforced.

tests.name: TestSandboxNamesFailuresFromEveryShard
tests.says: An assertion failure, panic, shard timeout or package build error fails the check and names the failed package, test and shard where applicable, while healthy shards and independent acceptance checks still complete.

tests.name: TestSandboxDeadlineReturnsPartialResults
tests.says: The sandbox's own deadline stops hung tests, vet or acceptance checks and removes the container, returning a failed result with completed, failed, running and unstarted tests distinguished and their names retained in the delivered summary.

tests.name: TestSandboxKeepsAcceptanceResultsByPackage
tests.says: Acceptance tests with the same function name in different packages retain their individual outcomes, so another package's passing test cannot satisfy a failing acceptance test.

tests.name: TestSandboxBudgetAndRealCheckout
tests.says: The sandbox deadline, startup reserve and cleanup reserve stay below the tool limits actually configured by every supported backend; an external plumbing_test test keeps this build's checks out of internal/verify, while its opt-in real-image subtest names internal/verify in its own plan and checks three concurrent cold-cache runs finish successfully within that budget with measured memory and process peaks below their enforced limits.
